header.running_head: The Fervour of the Sahabah (RA) to earn Rewards

blocks.text: note that the salaah of a sitting person is half (in reward) of the salaah of a standing person." Thereafter the Sahabah (RA) exerted themselves greatly to perform salaah while standing despite their extreme weakness and illness solely in aspiration for the additional rewards.[^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b (RA) with Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b (RA) says, "I was Rasulullaah ﷺ's servant and served him all day until he performed the Isha salaah. I would then sit by his door when he entered his room saying to myself, 'Perhaps Rasulullaah ﷺ will need something.' I would then remain sitting there hearing Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Subhaanallaahi wa Bi-hamdihi,' until I would get tired or until my eyes overwhelmed me and I would fall asleep right there. Seeing my fervour to serve him and feeling that he owed something to me, Rasulullaah ﷺ one day asked me, 'O Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b! Ask from me and I shall give you.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I submitted, 'Allow me to think about it and then I shall inform you.'
I then addressed myself saying, 'The things of this world are temporary and will soon come to an end. In any case, I have my (preordained) sustenance in this world which is sufficient for me and will come to me (it is therefore futile to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for some worldly thing). I shall therefore ask Rasulullaah ﷺ for something of benefit for my life in the Aakhirah because he enjoys an exalted status with Allaah.' I then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and he asked, 'What have you decided, O Rabee'ah?' 'I have made a decision, O Rasulullaah ﷺ,' I said, 'My request to you is to intercede on my behalf that Allaah frees me from Jahannam.' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'Who told you to say this, O Rabee'ah?' I explained to him saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that no one told me what to say. You asked me to ask from you and because you enjoy a high status in Allaah's sight, I though the matter over. Realising that the things of this world are temporary and will soon come to an end and that I have my (preordained) sustenance in this world which will come to me I decided to ask you for something of benefit for my life in the Aakhirah.' Rasulullaah ﷺ remained silent for a long while after which he said, 'I shall do that but do assist me against your carnal self by making Sajdah in abundance.'"[^2]

In another narration, Hadhrat Rabee'ah (RA) says, "I used to spend the night in the service of Rasulullaah ﷺ, bringing him his water for wudhu and seeing to his other needs. When he once asked me to make a request, I said, 'I request your company in Jannah.' 'Anything else?' he asked. When I insisted that this was all, he said, 'Then assist me against your carnal self by making Sajdah in abundance.'"[^3]
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.3 Pg.224).
Ahmad, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.335). Tabraani, Muslim and Abu Dawood have reported a similar narration in brief.
Muslim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.1 Pg.213).
